algorithm.summary: Builds the maximal legal schema-defined object for one IPC direction and returns its 4-byte big-endian frame length prefix as hex. Proves the payload-fit invariant: every payload legal under the transport contract is representable in BOTH directions under the 131,072-byte frame ceiling.
algorithm.canonical_form: Compact JSON (separators ',' and ':' with no spaces), keys in the order the schema declares them. The IPC contract does not pin a canonical JSON form because the ceiling is a bound rather than an equality; this fixture declares the form it measures instead of attributing one to the contract.
algorithm.scope: The measured object is the schema-defined one (ipc.send-params, endpoints.message-received). The outer request/event envelope is modelled by no schema, so its budget is reported as envelope_headroom_bytes rather than invented here.

vectors.name: send-params-maximal
vectors.note: The invariant's worst case for a command: 49,152 payload bytes plus every bounded v2 metadata field at its ceiling.

vectors.name: message-received-maximal
vectors.note: The worst case for the event direction, which carries both endpoints and is therefore the larger of the two.
